proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(m_G=1+d/\gamma\) and \(D_F=1+d/\gamma+d/q\).  Constants denoted by \(c\) and \(C\) below are positive, depend only on \(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,e_0\), and may change from line to line.

First, privacy cannot reduce the nonprivate minimax risk.  Let \(T\) be any pure \(\epsilon\)-differentially private Markov kernel from \(\mathcal O^n\) to \([-2,2]\), and define its conditional barycenter
\[
\overline T(D_n)=\int_{[-2,2]}t\,T(dt\mid D_n).
\]
The bounded output support makes this integral finite and puts \(\overline T(D_n)\in[-2,2]\).  Conditional Jensen's inequality gives, for every \(P\in\mathcal M_H\),
\[
|\overline T(D_n)-\theta(P)|
\le \int_{[-2,2]}|t-\theta(P)|\,T(dt\mid D_n).
\]
Taking expectation under \(P^{\otimes n}\), then the supremum over \(P\in\mathcal M_H\), shows that the risk of \(T\) is at least the risk of the nonprivate estimator \(\overline T\).  By \(\mathrm{def:nonprivate-risk}\), the latter supremum is at least \(R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\).  Infimizing over the private kernels in \(\mathrm{def:private-risk}\) therefore gives
\[
R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}\ge R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}. \tag{1}
\]

We next prove the dense privacy branch.  Fix a nonnegative \(C^\infty\) function \(g\), supported on \([-1,1]^d\), with \(0\le g\le1\) and \(g(0)=1\).  For a separation \(0<\Delta\le\Delta_0\), let
\[
h=c_h\Delta^{1/\gamma},\qquad
g_h(x)=g\!\left(\frac{x-x_0}{h}\right).
\]
Choose the fixed constant \(c_h>0\) so that the Hölder scaling bound \(\|\Delta g_h\|_{\mathcal H^\gamma}\le L\) holds, and then choose \(\Delta_0>0\) so that \(h\le1/4\).  Because \(x_0\in[1/4,3/4]^d\), the support of \(g_h\) is contained in \([0,1]^d\).

For \(j\in\{0,1\}\), construct \(P_j\) as follows.  Let \(X\) be uniform on \([0,1]^d\), let \(A\) be conditionally Bernoulli with \(\pi_j(x)=1/2\), set \(\mu_{0,j}(x)=0\), and set
\[
\tau_0(x)=0,\qquad \tau_1(x)=\Delta g_h(x),
\qquad \mu_{1,j}(x)=\mu_{0,j}(x)+\tau_j(x).
\]
Given \(X=x\), draw binary potential outcomes in \(\{-1,1\}\), independently of \(A\), with means \(\mu_{0,j}(x)\) and \(\mu_{1,j}(x)\), and impose \(Y=AY_1+(1-A)Y_0\).  This construction gives consistency and conditional exchangeability.  The uniform design, constant propensity, zero control regression, the displayed Hölder scaling, and \(e_0\le1/4\) verify every condition in \(\mathrm{def:holder-class}\); boundedness follows from \(0\le\Delta g_h\le1\) after decreasing \(\Delta_0\).  Thus \(P_0,P_1\in\mathcal M_H\), while
\[
\theta(P_0)=0,\qquad \theta(P_1)=\Delta. \tag{2}
\]

Couple one record from the two laws by using the same \(X\), the same \(A\), and a common uniform random variable to generate the two binary outcomes.  Conditional on \((X,A)\), a mismatch is impossible when \(A=0\), and when \(A=1\) its probability is the total variation distance between two Bernoulli laws, namely \(\Delta g_h(X)/2\).  Hence
\[
\Pr(O_0\ne O_1)
=\frac14\Delta\int_{[0,1]^d}g_h(x)\,dx
\le C\Delta h^d.
\]
Repeating this coupling independently over the \(n\) coordinates gives a coupling of \(P_0^{\otimes n}\) and \(P_1^{\otimes n}\) with expected Hamming distance
\[
D\le Cn\Delta h^d\le Cn\Delta^{m_G}. \tag{3}
\]
Under \(n\epsilon\ge1\), the cap in \(\rho_G\) is inactive and \(\rho_G^{m_G}=(n\epsilon)^{-1}\).  Set \(\Delta=c_G\rho_G\), where \(c_G>0\) is small enough that \(\Delta\le\Delta_0\) and, by (3), \(10\epsilon D\le1\).  Thresholding the output of any private estimator at \(\Delta/2\) is post-processing and hence is a pure \(\epsilon\)-private test.  Applying \(\mathrm{lem:private-le-cam-coupling}\) with privacy slack zero gives a testing error bounded below by the positive numerical constant \(0.45e^{-1}\).  By (2), a testing error forces absolute estimation loss at least \(\Delta/2\).  Taking the larger of the two risks and then infimizing over private estimators proves
\[
R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}\ge c\Delta\ge c\rho_G. \tag{4}
\]

It remains to prove the sparse-collision branch.  Suppose first that \(\rho_F\ge\rho_G\).  The regime \(n\epsilon\ge1\), together with \(n\ge1\) and \(\epsilon\le1\), makes both caps inactive, so
\[
\rho_F^{D_F}=(n^2\epsilon)^{-1},
\qquad
\rho_G^{m_G}=(n\epsilon)^{-1}. \tag{5}
\]
We claim that \(n\rho_F^{d/q}\le1\).  Otherwise, (5) would give
\[
\rho_F^{m_G}
=\frac{\rho_F^{D_F}}{\rho_F^{d/q}}
<\frac1{n\epsilon}
=\rho_G^{m_G},
\]
contradicting \(\rho_F\ge\rho_G\) because \(m_G>0\).  This proves the claim.

Set \(\Delta=c_F\rho_F\), with \(c_F>0\) fixed and sufficiently small.  Apply \(\mathrm{lem:two-fiber-distance-certificate}\) with comparison constants chosen so that
\[
h\asymp\Delta^{1/\gamma},\qquad
\ell\asymp\Delta^{1/q},\qquad
n\ell^d\le c_0.
\]
The last inequality is valid because \(n\rho_F^{d/q}\le1\) and \(c_F\) can absorb the fixed comparison constant in \(\ell\asymp\Delta^{1/q}\).  The lemma supplies two priors supported on laws in \(\mathcal M_H\), with target values \(\Delta\) and zero, whose prior-predictive sample laws admit a coupling satisfying
\[
D\le C\Delta n^2h^d\ell^d
\le Cn^2\Delta^{D_F}. \tag{6}
\]
By (5),
\[
\epsilon D\le C\epsilon n^2c_F^{D_F}\rho_F^{D_F}
=Cc_F^{D_F}.
\]
Choose \(c_F\) still smaller so that \(10\epsilon D\le1\).  The private coupling lemma, now applied to the two convex hulls carrying the priors, and midpoint thresholding as above yield
\[
R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}\ge c\Delta\ge c\rho_F. \tag{7}
\]
This also proves the witness assertion in the theorem: the certificate gives smooth shared-sign two-fiber mixtures, the stated scales, the sparse occupancy bound, and the Hamming cost in (6).  If instead \(\rho_F<\rho_G\), (4) immediately implies a constant multiple of \(\rho_F\), so no separate sparse witness is required in that regime.

Equations (1), (4), and (7) give fixed positive lower multiples of \(R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\), \(\rho_G\), and \(\rho_F\), respectively.  Taking the minimum of their three constants proves
\[
R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}
\ge c_{\mathrm{lower}}
\left(R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F\right),
\]
as claimed.

added_lemmas.statement:
Every law in the exact-uniform class belongs to the Kennedy-Theorem-1 slice:
\[
\mathcal M_H\subseteq\mathcal P_K.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M_H\).  By \(\mathrm{def:holder-class}\), the law has the support declared in the definition of \(\mathcal P_K\), satisfies consistency and conditional exchangeability, obeys the overlap bound with constant \(e_0\), and has
\[
\pi\in\mathcal H^\alpha(L),\qquad
\mu_0\in\mathcal H^\beta(L),\qquad
\tau\in\mathcal H^\gamma(L),
\qquad q=\alpha+\beta<\gamma.
\]
The only remaining membership condition is the design-density condition.  By \(\mathrm{ass:uniform-design}\), \(P_X\) has Lebesgue density one on \([0,1]^d\).  Since \(L\ge2\), this density satisfies
\[
0\le \frac{dP_X}{d\lambda_d}(x)=1\le L
\]
for \(\lambda_d\)-almost every \(x\).  This verifies the bounded-above condition in \(\mathrm{def:kennedy-lower-class}\).  Notice that the argument neither invokes nor proves a global density lower bound for a generic member of \(\mathcal P_K\).  Hence \(P\in\mathcal P_K\), and arbitrariness of \(P\) proves the inclusion.
added_lemmas.justification: This inclusion is the complete order-theoretic bridge needed to transfer every exact-uniform minimax lower branch to the Kennedy-Theorem-1 slice.
added_lemmas.gap: The transfer is invalid unless the two model classes are explicitly defined and their inclusion is checked without importing a density lower bound.
added_lemmas.consumer: The superclass lower-frontier theorem uses this lemma before taking the infimum over the common private-estimator set.

added_lemmas.statement:
There is a constant \(c_K>0\), depending only on \(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,e_0\), such that throughout \(n\epsilon\ge1\),
\[
R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP},K}
\ge c_K\left[
\left\{n^{-1/(2+d/\gamma)}\vee
n^{-2/(2+d/\gamma+d/q)}\right\}
\vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F
\right].
\]
This is an upward transfer of lower bounds from \(\mathcal M_H\) to the Kennedy-Theorem-1 slice \(\mathcal P_K\); it makes no upper-bound assertion over \(\mathcal P_K\).
added_lemmas.justification: The theorem turns the exact-uniform converse into an explicit pure-private lower frontier on the larger Kennedy-Theorem-1 density class.
added_lemmas.gap: Kennedy et al. establish a nonprivate lower bound, while the two privacy branches require the exact-uniform causal constructions and an explicit superclass monotonicity argument.
added_lemmas.consumer: It supports comparator positioning on Kennedy et al.'s lower-bound class without transferring the still-conditional exact-uniform upper bound.

proposed.name: Kennedy-Theorem-1 lower-bound slice
proposed.construction:
The class \(\mathcal P_K\) is the \(q=\alpha+\beta<\gamma\) common-support and common-constant causal slice of the lower-bound model in Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024), Theorem~1:
\[
\begin{split}
\mathcal P_K=\bigl\{P:\;&P\text{ is a law on }(X,A,Y_0,Y_1,Y)\text{ with }X\in[0,1]^d,
\ A\in\{0,1\},\ Y_0,Y_1,Y\in[-1,1],\\
&Y=AY_1+(1-A)Y_0\text{ almost surely},\qquad
Y_a\perp A\mid X\text{ for }a\in\{0,1\},\\
&P_X\ll\lambda_d,\quad
0\le \frac{dP_X}{d\lambda_d}(x)\le L
\text{ for }\lambda_d\text{-almost every }x\in[0,1]^d,\\
&e_0\le\pi(x)\le1-e_0\text{ for every }x\in[0,1]^d,\quad
\pi\in\mathcal H^\alpha(L),\quad
\mu_0\in\mathcal H^\beta(L),\quad
\tau\in\mathcal H^\gamma(L)\bigr\},
\end{split}
\]
where \(\lambda_d\) denotes Lebesgue measure on \([0,1]^d\), \(x_0\in[1/4,3/4]^d\), and the parameters obey \(q=\alpha+\beta<\gamma\).  No positive lower bound on \(dP_X/d\lambda_d\) is imposed.

proposed_core_edits.reason: This definition records exactly the common-support/constants slice needed for upward transfer and imposes only the published bounded-above design-density condition, not a density lower bound or Theorem~2's attainability conditions.

proposed.name: Pure-private minimax risk over the Kennedy-Theorem-1 slice

proposed_core_edits.reason: Minimax monotonicity is meaningful only after the superclass risk is defined over the identical estimator and privacy domain.

proposed.statement:
There is a constant \(c_{\mathrm{lower}}>0\), depending only on
\(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,e_0\), such that throughout \(n\epsilon\ge1\),
\[
 R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}
 \ge c_{\mathrm{lower}}\{R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F\}.
\]
The \(\rho_G\) term is witnessed by a localized one-record subexperiment.
For the \(\rho_F\) term, whenever \(\rho_F\ge\rho_G\), there are smooth
shared-sign two-fiber mixtures in \(\mathcal M_H\), separated by
\(\delta\asymp\rho_F\), whose prior-predictive samples admit a coupling with
expected Hamming distance at most
\(C\delta n^2h^d\ell^d\), where
\(h\asymp\delta^{1/\gamma}\),
\(\ell\asymp\delta^{1/q}\), and \(n\ell^d\le C\).  If
\(\rho_F<\rho_G\), the \(\rho_F\) lower bound is already implied by the
\(\rho_G\) branch.
proposed.justification: The unconditional exact-uniform converse establishes both privacy radii on the same causal class and supplies the lower-bound input for upward superclass transfer.
proposed.gap: Kennedy et al. give the nonprivate term, and Acharya et al. give a generic coupling inequality; neither supplies the localized causal experiments proving the dense and sparse pure-private branches.
proposed.consumer: The result lower-bounds any prospective exact-uniform upper mechanism and, through explicit class inclusion, every private estimator over the Kennedy-Theorem-1 slice.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The claim is unchanged, but the reissued proof uses the frozen two-fiber distance certificate as a load-bearing sparse-branch dependency, which must be declared explicitly.

proposed_core_edits.proposed:
Unconditionally on the exact-uniform class,
\[
R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}
\gtrsim R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F.
\]
For the Kennedy-Theorem-1 slice,
\[
R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP},K}
\gtrsim
\left\{n^{-1/(2+d/\gamma)}\vee
n^{-2/(2+d/\gamma+d/(\alpha+\beta))}\right\}
\vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F.
\]
Only conditional on an affirmative resolution of Open-ended Question~1 does the exact-uniform relation strengthen to
\[
R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}
\asymp R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F.
\]
proposed_core_edits.reason: The previous display stated a matched exact-uniform frontier unconditionally.  The corrected metadata distinguishes the unconditional exact-uniform and superclass lower bounds from the exact-uniform upper bound conditional on Open-ended Question~1.

proposed.comparator_claim: Theorem~1 gives the nonprivate pointwise Hölder-CATE lower bound on a class whose covariate density is bounded above; Theorem~2 treats attainability under separate estimator and design conditions.
Section~4 uses treated--control occupancy and effect homogeneity to obtain a global nonprivate rate with a collision term.
The paper stabilizes central-private U-statistics using local Hájek projections and tuple reweighting.
Section~4 gives a general pure-private T-mechanism based on clipped likelihood-ratio tests and finite covers.
The paper gives central-private Le Cam, Fano, and Assouad inequalities based on expected Hamming transport.
Theorems~1 and~3 give finite-query and functional observational CATE releases under approximate differential privacy.
The sparse-histogram lower bound and compact dense-histogram theorem show that pure-private costs can change with representation and occupancy.
Their multiscale and adaptive-lower-bound arguments are templates for the separate unresolved adaptation question; no adaptive rate or logarithmic penalty is imported here.
The paper establishes nonprivate heterogeneous-effect minimax rates with explicit random-design geometry.
Definition~2 and Section~4 construct T-estimators from coherent tests on countable model nets.

prose_updates.tldr: The occupancy-weighted score has an unconditional exact expectation and constant replacement sensitivity, while the exact-uniform Hölder class has unconditional dense \(\rho_G\) and sparse \(\rho_F\) pure-private lower branches in addition to its nonprivate minimax floor.  Because the exact-uniform class is contained in the common-support/constants slice of Kennedy et al.'s Theorem~1 lower-bound class, all of these lower branches transfer upward and yield an explicit superclass converse.  A matching upper bound remains conditional on the unresolved full-fiber occupancy lift on the exact-uniform class, and smoothness adaptation remains wholly open; no adaptive rate or logarithmic penalty is claimed.

project_justification.fill: The project proves the occupancy identity and the sparse and dense pure-private lower branches unconditionally on the exact-uniform class, then transfers the resulting converse upward to the Kennedy-Theorem-1 bounded-above-density slice.  Matching attainment on the exact-uniform class remains conditional on the unresolved full-fiber occupancy lift, and the separate adaptation problem remains open with no claimed logarithmic penalty.

prose_updates.related_work: Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman's Theorem~1 gives the nonprivate pointwise Hölder-CATE lower bound on a class requiring the covariate density only to be bounded above.  Their Theorem~2 addresses attainability under separate estimator and design conditions, including additional local-support requirements; the two theorems are not treated here as defining one class.  The present exact-uniform class is a subclass of the common-support/constants Theorem~1 slice: the causal two-fiber constructions prove the dense and sparse privacy lower branches on that subclass, and minimax monotonicity transfers every lower branch upward.  No upper bound is transferred.  Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy motivate conditioning on realized occupancy; Chaudhuri, Loh, Pandey, and Sarkar motivate stable local projections; and Acharya, Sun, and Zhang supply the private Hamming-coupling inequality used in the converse.  Birgé and Asi, Duchi, Haque, Li, and Ruan provide test-selection templates for the unresolved exact-uniform upper construction.  Schröder, Melnychuk, and Feuerriegel study approximate-private CATE releases rather than this pure-private minimax problem.  Balcer and Vadhan illustrate sparse--dense privacy transitions.  Cai, Chakraborty, and Vuursteen provide templates only for a separate open adaptation question: this note claims neither an adaptive rate nor a logarithmic adaptation penalty.  Gao and Han analyze distinct nonprivate random-design geometry.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The unconditional results are the occupancy identity, the nonprivate floor, and the dense and sparse pure-private lower branches on the fixed-smoothness exact-uniform class, together with their upward lower-bound transfer to the common-support/constants slice of Kennedy et al.'s Theorem~1 class, whose design density is bounded above but need not be bounded below.  No superclass upper bound is asserted.  The matching upper frontier on the exact-uniform class is explicitly conditional on resolving the full-fiber occupancy lift, and smoothness adaptation is wholly open; no adaptive rate or logarithmic penalty is claimed.
